title: Priv: IAM/RBAC Terraform module — scaffold, least-privilege templates, and upgrade safety
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Build a reusable Terraform module and accompanying repo patterns for provisioning IAM and RBAC for Private (VPC) deployments that enforces least-privilege by default, provides upgrade-safe migration patterns, and includes automated health checks and CI gates.

Scope:
- A single Terraform module (aws/google/azurerm variants) that creates: IAM roles, role bindings/service accounts, constrained assume-role/assume-service-account policies, and optional permission templates for common Redwood services (console, runtime agent, metrics exporter).
- A least-privilege policy generator (CLI/Make task) that consumes a service's required API surface (list of actions/resources) and emits provider policy JSONs compatible with the module.
- Upgrade safety: versioned module inputs, a migration playbook, canary apply patterns, automated pre/post plan checks, and Terraform state migration helpers.
- Health checks: a lightweight test harness (kitchen/terratest style) and a set of runtime probes that validate role assumptions, KMS decrypt permissions, and audit logging access after apply.
- CI integration: plan/validate/lint step, policy diff checks (deny-on-broad-permissions), and a smoke test stage that runs against a sandbox VPC.

Non-goals:
- Full permission discovery for arbitrary third-party workloads (we provide a templated workflow and guardrails).
- Replacing cloud-native IAM governance tools (we integrate with them via labels and tags).

Deliverables:
- Terraform module repo with examples for staging and production patterns.
- CLI generator and sample permission profiles.
- Upgrade playbook and checklist (docs + executable scripts).
- CI pipeline jobs added to the infra repo for plan/validate/health-checks.

Constraints & assumptions:
- Primary first target: AWS. GCP and Azure variants are scoped as follow-ups.
- Customers/private instances require minimal blast radius by default (namespaced roles/scoped policies).
- We must maintain compatibility with existing state files for customers using older IAM modules — module will include optional compatibility flags.
acceptance_criteria: Module published to internal registry with semver tags and example usage for staging and prod
Least-privilege generator produces policies that pass a deny-on-broad-permissions CI rule
Upgrade playbook exercises a canary apply path and rollback instructions documented
Automated health checks (role-assume, kms-decrypt, logging-write) run in CI and pass against sandbox
Security review completed and sign-off recorded
Migration helper scripts for common state changes included and tested

implementation_notes: Module pattern: separate role definition (core) from permission attachment (policy module) so policies can be rotated without replacing roles
Provide optional 'managed_by' tag for integration with org-level governance tools
Expose 'assume_conditions' to restrict role usage by source IP/VPC endpoint where supported
Use provider-agnostic outputs (json_policy, role_arn) for downstream modules
Include an examples/ directory with terraform workspaces for 'sandbox', 'staging', and 'prod' patterns
risks_mitigations: Risk: Overly-broad policies shipped by mistake. Mitigation: CI denies any policy containing '/*' resources or 'iam:*' and runs policy-sentry style checks.
Risk: State migration causing customer downtime. Mitigation: require dry-run on customer staging and provide tfstate-backed rename helpers + manual approval gate.
Risk: KMS decrypt timing/clash in CI. Mitigation: add retry logic in health checks and ensure KMS keys are created with predictable aliases in examples.
